In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cage-type structure is the most stable structure for NH(4)(+)(H(2O))4 at room temperature and that the open structure is the most probable structure for NH(+)4(H2O)(6) at room temperature.

the most stable structure of NH(4)(+) (H(2) O)(n=4-6) is not the cage-type structure but the open structure, and the cage-type structure is not the most stable structure but one of the lowest energy isomers.
the cage-type structure for NH(4)(+) (H2O)6 is less stable than the open structure by about 2 kcal/mol and that the experimental IR spectrum is best reproduced by the cage-type structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified the most stable structures for NH( 4) (+)( H(2)O) n=4, 6 and that we can explain the experimental IR spectrum by the power spectra obtained by first principles molecular dynamics simulation.

the first principles Car-Parninello molecular dynamics calculations are useful for the assignment of IR spectra of NH(4)(+)(H(2))O)(n=2,4,6) and that the ZPE correction to the CCSD(T)/CBS binding energy is necessary to determine the most stable structures of NH(4(+))(H(2) O)(n=2-6).

the most important structural isomers of (NH(4) (+))(n=4,5,6)(H(2)) are identified and their vibrational spectra are explained by using the combination of ab initio calculations and the first principles molecular dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ZPE correction is crucial for identifying the low energy structures of NH(4)(+) (H(2)0)(n) clusters, and the combined power spectrum from the first principles molecular dynamics simulation explains the experimental IR spectra of NH(4(+)) (H(2)(O))(4,6).
the experimental IR spectrum of NH(4)(+) (H(2) O)(4) is not consistent with the cage-type structure but with the open structure.
the first principles Car-Parninello molecular dynamics simulation with a proper initial configuration is an efficient tool to identify the most probable structures for the clusters of interest.
